1.title: Storage Accounts: Redundancy, Replication and Encryption
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Storage Accounts: Redundancy, Replication and Encryption. It covers the exam area Implement and manage storage. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Create and configure storage accounts. Configure Azure Storage redundancy. Configure object replication. Configure storage account encryption. Manage data by using Azure Storage Explorer and Az Copy. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement and manage storage (fifteen-twenty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: The storage account
1.text: The storage account. An Azure storage account is a namespace (a unique name, name dot blob dot core dot windows dot net ) that holds your storage services. Blob. Objects (files, images, backups). Files. File shares (S M B, N F S (Network File System)). Queue. Messages between application components. Table. No sequel key-attribute data.

1.title: The storage account, continued
1.text: The storage account. Standard general-purpose version two. Default for most uses (all services). Premium block blobs. Low latency for blobs. Premium file shares. High-performance file shares. Premium page blobs. V M disks (unmanaged) and page blobs. The account name must be globally unique (three to twenty-four lowercase letters and numbers). Region, performance and redundancy are chosen at creation.

1.title: Redundancy
1.text: Redundancy. The figure shows this: Storage redundancy options: L R S (locally redundant storage), Z R S (zone-redundant storage), G R S (geo-redundant storage), G Z R S (geo-zone-redundant storage) and read-access variants.

1.title: Redundancy, continued
1.text: Redundancy. L R S (locally redundant). Copies and location: three copies in one datacenter. Protects against: Disk or rack failure. Z R S (zone-redundant). Copies and location: three copies across three availability zones in the region. Protects against: A datacenter (zone) failure. G R S (geo-redundant). Copies and location: L R S in the primary region plus asynchronous copy (L R S) to a secondary region. Protects against: A regional outage.

1.title: Redundancy, continued
1.text: Redundancy. G Z R S (geo-zone-redundant). Copies and location: Z R S in the primary plus L R S in the secondary region. Protects against: Zone and regional failure. R A G R S or R A G Z R S. Copies and location: As G R S or G Z R S, plus read access to the secondary endpoint. Protects against: Regional outage with read availability. Exam tip: Zone failure only equals Z R S. Region failure equals G R S or G Z R S. Need to read from the secondary region equals R A G R S or R A G Z R S. Secondary data is replicated asynchronously, so a failover can lose recent writes. You can change redundancy after creation (some conversions need a migration request).

1.title: Object replication
1.text: Object replication. Object replication asynchronously copies block blobs from a source container to a destination container, in another account or region, according to rules (with optional prefix filters). Prerequisites. Blob versioning enabled on both accounts, change feed on the source. Direction. One-way per rule (source to destination). Use. Lower latency for readers in another region, data distribution, compliance copies.

1.title: Encryption
1.text: Encryption. At rest. Always on: all data is encrypted with two hundred fifty-six-bit A E S; cannot be turned off. Keys. Microsoft-managed keys (default) or customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault (or Managed H S M). Infrastructure encryption. Optional second layer of encryption. In transit. Secure transfer required forces H T T P S (and S M B (Server Message Block) encryption for Files); set the minimum T L S version. Exam tip: "Control the encryption keys" equals customer-managed keys in Key Vault.

1.title: Storage Explorer and AzCopy
1.text: Storage Explorer and Az Copy. Azure Storage Explorer. gooey app to browse and manage blobs, files, queues and tables. Az Copy. Command-line tool to copy and sync data quickly: azcopy login, azcopy copy, azcopy sync; authenticate with Entra I D or a S A S token. Exam tip: Storage encryption at rest cannot be turned off; the question is only who holds the keys (Microsoft or you in Key Vault).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An application must keep data available if one datacenter in the region fails, with the lowest cost that meets this. Which option fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Z R S. Z R S spreads copies across availability zones in the region.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company needs to read data from the secondary region during a regional outage. Which option fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: R A G R S. Read-access variants allow reads from the secondary endpoint.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A team wants to copy new blobs automatically to a storage account in another region. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Object replication. Object replication copies block blobs between accounts asynchronously.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which prerequisites does object replication need? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Blob versioning, and change feed on the source. Versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source are required.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team wants control of the keys that encrypt a storage account. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault. Customer-managed keys give control over the encryption keys.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An administrator needs to copy two T B of blobs between accounts from the command line. Which tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Az Copy. Az Copy copies and syncs large data sets.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many copies does L R S keep, and where? Answer: Three, in one datacenter. Question two. What does Z R S protect against? Answer: The failure of one availability zone (datacenter). Question three. What does R A in R A G R S add? Answer: Read access to the secondary region.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Can storage encryption at rest be turned off? Answer: No, it is always on. Question five. Name the four storage services. Answer: Blob, Files, Queue and Table. Question six. What does secure transfer required enforce? Answer: H T T P S for requests to the account.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Services: Blob, Files, Queue, Table; general-purpose version two is the default. Redundancy: L R S (datacenter), Z R S (zones), G R S (region), G Z R S (zones plus region), R A- for read access. Object replication: async block blobs; versioning plus change feed. Encryption: always on at rest; customer-managed keys in Key Vault; secure transfer. Tools: Storage Explorer (gooey), Az Copy (command line).
